indication.text: Treatment of moderate to severe acute pain in adults

target_moa.text: Selective blocker of the voltage-gated sodium channel subtype 1.8 (Nav1.8), which is predominantly expressed in peripheral sensory neurons including dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, suppressing action potential firing and reducing pain signaling

citations.quote: SUZ is a selective blocker of the Na_v1.8 voltage-gated sodium channel compared to other known voltage-gated sodium channels (i.e., Na_v1.1 through 1.9). Na_v1.8 is predominantly expressed in peripheral sensory neurons, including dorsal root ganglion (DR

SUZ selectively inhibits a voltage-gated sodium channel subtype 1.8 (\text{Na}_v 1.8), which is expressed in DRG neurons, suppressing action potential firing in DRG neurons and reducing pain signaling.

modality.text: Small molecule (new molecular entity; sodium channel blocker)

citations.quote: SUZ is a new molecular entity with a mechanism of action of blocking the voltage-gated sodium channel Na_v1.8 currents.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (greater incidence vs placebo) were pruritus (2.1% vs 1.6% placebo), muscle spasms (1.3% vs 0.5%), increased blood creatine phosphokinase (1.1% vs 0.5%), and rash (1.1% vs 0.5%). Serious adverse events were generally consistent with known postoperative complications of surgery and their incidence was low and balanced between treatment arms.

requirement.text: 4787-7 Collect global data from prospective pregnancy exposure registry/registries, preferably disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry/registries, using a registry-based cohort study design to compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Journavx during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s).

citations.quote: 4787-7 Collect global data from prospective pregnancy exposure registry/registries, preferably disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry/registries, using a registry-based cohort study design to compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Journavx during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s). Align the U.S. study protocol with protocol(s) outside the U.S. to reach the target sample size. The registry will identify and record pregnancy complications, spontaneous abortion, stillbirths, neonatal deaths, major and minor congenital malformations, pregnancy terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. These outcomes should be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.
